headline: The booth keeps its case on screen
lede: Papers, Please-Min's verdict used to fade with the ink — half a second for a three-clause deny. Now the stamp mark rides the paper, the witness and evidence clauses stay pinned through a two-second read window, and the inspector is dismissed exactly when the next applicant's papers land on your counter.

notes.text: THE INSPECTOR STAYS — after you stamp, the judged document holds the counter while the case stays readable: gold witness for what you caught, red for what you missed. Stamp earlier and the hand-off snaps to your cadence; input is never blocked.
The paper drop moved behind the read window: the next entrant's papers now fall only when the case is done being shown — the wall never quotes yesterday's reason behind today's face.

Gates grew with it: paperscheck 17614 with 42 mutants dead (new m42 shrinks the pin below the 2 s read-window law), papersplay 85/85 live, including two new lifetime gates that prove the pin in pixels — and that a stuck pin goes red.
